flight_records.method: Dense strips (every 2nd frame, 400 px thumbs), wing-phase read frame by frame
flight_records.neck: Folded into the cruise S throughout; no takeoff in this clip.
flight_records.verdict: RATE-SUSPECT: a ~2.3 s wingbeat cannot sustain flight; the Boga clips behave like high-fps sources conformed slow (factor unknown; ~5-6x would put the true rate at the expected ~2.5 Hz). Publish render-domain only. Flap-glide structure visible in the same window (level-wing glides of ~0.5-1 s render between bouts).

meta.method: Same instruments as main study: torso = max pairwise distance among tail-tip/chest-front/back-top/belly (hull-diameter); skull = midpoint(eye, back-of-head); chain skull -> neck points -> neckbase; arc = polyline length; station-1 = point at 76% of arc; chord76 = |skull -> station-1|; chord_base = |skull -> neckbase|. Coordinates are 0-1000 image units (visual_grounding), converted to px with the frame's real W x H. Near-profile only for pooled length ratios; oblique sets kept as flagged floors. Slow-mo / rate-unknown renders contribute ratios or structure only, never absolute timings.
meta.note_on_midpoints: Addendum sets carry ONE mid-neck point (front-edge convention) vs the study's denser chains; arc and chord76 on coiled frames are therefore FLOORS. On near-straight peak frames the bias is negligible (57Y peak polyline exceeds straight chord by 0.4%).

stretch_record.context: Bird lands in a pine at ~16-17.5 s; the spread follows the landing settle - it is a POST-LANDING wing-spread hold, not a separate stretch routine.
stretch_record.form: BOTH wings extend together, symmetrically, to full horizontal span with primaries fanned; neck stays up, no neck extension; no stepping (contrast the landing-balance spread, which is asymmetric and stepped).
stretch_record.rate_note: Boga rate-suspect; durations render-domain (30 fps render).

strike_timelines.class: standing spear, native 30 fps, near-profile; TORSO OUT OF FRAME - timing/profile only
strike_timelines.smoothing_note: Base-of-neck groundings drift +/-30-60 units on the blurred frames; f19/f20 chords smoothed to ~279/~356 in the profile computation.
strike_timelines.withdrawal: 58% of peak chord recovered by f33 (+0.40 s after peak); head then stays low for prey handling. Catch: small fish held by t~11 s, still repositioning through 19-22 s window (window-diff max at 19.47 s = handling, not a second strike).

swallow_timeline.note: For this SMALL fish (~0.25 torso), visible neck expansion is mostly the fish's own width; no large distension ratio is claimed (contrast the study's grey-heron 1.31/1.53 on larger prey).
swallow_timeline.rate_note: 24 fps render of a 120p source - all times render-domain; if conformed 5x, divide by 5.

underwater_record.observations: Split-level/underwater camera. Fish school 0-2 s; head/neck slash + first leg enter ~2.0-2.5 s; by 3.0 s BOTH legs are in, staggered in depth, near-vertical (within ~10-15 deg of vertical), feet spaced ~15% of frame width apart. Thereafter the bird simply WALKS through the frame on long legs (3.5-16 s), stirring sediment clouds - one plunge, no repeated striking. Leg-segment proportions could not be normalized (body above the surface, no torso ruler in the underwater frame).
